rows.label: Average household size, United States (persons per consumer unit)

source.title: BLS, Consumer Expenditures in 2024 (report), Table 2
source.quote: Average number in consumer unit: Persons 2.4

rows.explainer: Persons per consumer unit in the US Consumer Expenditure Survey, 2024 (a consumer unit is close to a household: the people who share their income and spending). The site's one figure for US household size.

rows.label: Average household size, lowest-income fifth of US households, 2024 (persons per consumer unit)

source.title: BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey via FRED, series CXU980010LB0102M (lowest quintile of income before taxes: average number in consumer unit)

rows.explainer: Persons per consumer unit among the poorest fifth of US households: fewer than the average (2.4), so per person their spending is a larger share of the average person's than per household. With @united_states.ce_lowest_quintile_vs_all_2024 it gives the poorest fifth's consumption per person against the average (0.446 × 2.4 / 1.6 = 0.67), the anchor for a US social service's clients.
